currentCoordinate.coordSource: Lovdata inventory 1 – Hovedfortet; Forsvarsbygg landsverneplan; OpenStreetMap relation 972050 – Hovedfortet; Riksantikvaren protection scope
currentCoordinate.coordNote: The canonical point is the deterministic multipolygon centroid of Hovedfortet on Søndre Kaholmen. Hovedbatteriet and the protected Torpedobatteriet on Nordre Kaholmen are retained as explicit secondary historical anchors inside the enlarged 520-metre gameplay radius.

previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: The rounded legacy point was plausible for the space between the Kaholmene but had no stable source identity or deterministic derivation. Raw geometry now supports Hovedfortet as the central historic and visitor-core anchor.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The dispersed historic fortress system in Drøbaksundet, represented canonically by Hovedfortet on Søndre Kaholmen with Hovedbatteriet and Torpedobatteriet as secondary anchors for the decisive island-core functions.
identity.identityProblem: Oscarsborg spans more than one hundred protected objects across the Kaholmene, other islands and mainland positions. A single legal-area centroid would misrepresent the destination, while one generic point cannot express the decisive 9 April functions.
identity.splitReason: The Kaholmene visitor core can remain one canonical destination through a main Hovedfortet marker and role-specific secondary anchors. Remote mainland batteries such as Seiersten are already separate or remain contextual candidates.

requiredEvidence: official fortress scope and Kaholmene core hierarchy
physical Torpedobatteriet cluster cross-check without invented underground polygon
explicit rejection of generic fortress points as canonical
explicit separation of remote mainland batteries

evidence.sourceName: Lovdata – protection regulation for Oscarsborg Fortress
evidence.finding: The regulation identifies inventory 1 as Hovedfortet with the coastal-fort sections, built 1849–1856, and protects all parts of the fort exterior and interior on gnr./bnr. 75/1.
evidence.reason: Defines the protected historical object represented by the canonical OSM geometry.

evidence.finding: Forsvarsbygg describes Søndre Kaholmen as containing the central and oldest parts of Oscarsborg, with Hovedfortet and Hovedbatteriet, while Nordre Kaholmen contains the Torpedobatteriet and other installations.
evidence.reason: Supports Hovedfortet as the central canonical anchor and the multi-anchor island model.

evidence.finding: Relation 972050 is named Hovedfortet and tagged building=yes, historic=fort, tourism=attraction and type=multipolygon. Materialized outer and inner rings yield centroid 59.67346966441094, 10.607055536295166.
evidence.reason: Provides the stable named physical geometry and deterministic point derivation required by the prior source audit.

evidence.finding: The named Hovedbatteriet bunker polygon has centroid 59.67263765222266, 10.607828593105598, approximately 102.2 metres from Hovedfortet.
evidence.reason: Secondary 9 April artillery anchor; it does not replace the complete fortress-core marker.

evidence.finding: The regulation identifies inventory 1018 as Torpedobatteri, built 1898–1901, with exterior and interior protected on gnr./bnr. 75/1.
evidence.reason: Defines the protected underground secondary component without implying an unsupported surface polygon.

evidence.finding: The named Torpedobatteriet memorial point at 59.6777982, 10.6077141 lies inside a physical cluster containing a 1901 steel door, underground service tunnel, three torpedo-battery sight towers, the Torpedobatteriverkstedet, a bunker and a bunker described as storage for torpedo warheads.
evidence.reason: Supports a semantic secondary anchor for protected inventory 1018 while explicitly avoiding invented underground geometry.

evidence.finding: The protection covers more than one hundred objects across Nordre and Søndre Kaholmen, Jetéen, Nesset, Bergholmen, Husvik, Kopås, Seiersten, Kringerud, Heer and selected Håøya installations.
evidence.reason: Demonstrates why neither the 520-metre gameplay circle nor one area centroid can represent the complete legal fortress landscape.

evidence.finding: The two generic same-name points lie near Hovedfortet but do not provide the deterministic geometry or explicit object role now available from relation 972050.
evidence.reason: Rejected as canonical in favor of the named Hovedfortet multipolygon.

evidence.finding: Kopåsbatteriet is approximately 920 metres from Hovedfortet and lies outside the 520-metre Kaholmene core radius.
evidence.reason: Important 9 April context, but geographically separate from the canonical island-core circle.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate 59.676, 10.606 is approximately 287.5 metres north-west of the Hovedfortet centroid and had no stable source identity or deterministic derivation.
evidence.reason: Replaced now that the required raw core geometry and multi-anchor policy are available.

decision.nextAction: Applied Hovedfortet as the canonical historical anchor, retained Hovedbatteriet and Torpedobatteriet as secondary anchors, and excluded remote mainland batteries from the Kaholmene core radius. Continue with trandumskogen.

notes: The canonical point moves approximately 287.5 metres from the rounded legacy point to Hovedfortet.
The radius increases to 520 metres because Hovedbatteriet is 102.2 metres and Torpedobatteriet is 482.7 metres from Hovedfortet.
The 520-metre circle is a gameplay representation of the key Kaholmene core, not the legal protected landscape.
No exact underground polygon is invented for the Torpedobatteriet.
Kopås, Seiersten, Heer, Nesset, Håøya and other remote components remain outside the canonical island-core circle.
